variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
section .data
    count dq 10       ; initialized 64-bit variable
    pi    dd 3.14159  ; initialized 32-bit float

section .bss
    buffer resb 64    ; uninitialized 64-byte buffer
variables.notes: Variables are memory allocations defined in sections (`.data` for initialized, `.bss` for uninitialized). Registers are used for temporary variables.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
db 0xAA        ; 8-bit byte
dw 0x1234      ; 16-bit word
dd 0x12345678  ; 32-bit double word
dq 0x11223344  ; 64-bit quad word
data_types.notes: Assembly has no structural types; data is simply bytes in memory. The programmer interprets size (db, dw, dd, dq).

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
mov rax, 10    ; Assignment
add rax, 5     ; Addition (rax = rax + 5)
sub rax, 2     ; Subtraction
and rax, 0xFF  ; Bitwise AND
xor rax, rax   ; Bitwise XOR (clears to 0)
operators.notes: Operations are CPU instructions mutating registers or memory directly, rather than mathematical expressions.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
cmp rax, 5
    jg .greater    ; Jump if greater
    je .equal      ; Jump if equal
    ; Lesser code here
    jmp .done
.greater:
    ; Greater code here
.equal:
.done:
conditionals.notes: Conditionals use a compare instruction (`cmp`) which sets CPU flags, followed by conditional jumps (`je`, `jg`, `jl`).

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.code:
mov rcx, 5     ; Loop counter
.loop_start:
    ; Loop body here
    dec rcx        ; Decrement counter
    jnz .loop_start; Jump if not zero
for_loop.notes: Loops are constructed manually using counters (often `rcx`), decrement instructions, and conditional jumps. The `loop` instruction exists but is often slower.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.code:
.while_start:
    cmp rax, 10
    jge .while_end ; Exit loop if rax >= 10
    
    inc rax        ; Loop body
    jmp .while_start
.while_end:
while_loop.notes: While loops test the condition before executing the body, jumping over the body if the condition is false.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
my_add:
    ; Inputs in rdi, rsi (System V AMD64 ABI)
    lea rax, [rdi + rsi] ; rax = rdi + rsi
    ret

    ; Call it
    mov rdi, 2
    mov rsi, 3
    call my_add
functions.notes: Functions are just labeled memory addresses called with `call` and exited with `ret`. Arguments are passed via registers according to an OS-specific ABI.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.code:
section .data
    arr dq 10, 20, 30, 40

section .text
    ; Access arr[2] (index * 8 bytes for dq)
    mov rax, [arr + 2*8]
arrays.notes: Arrays are continuous blocks of memory. Access requires manual address arithmetic by multiplying the index by the element size.

maps.title: Maps
maps.code:
; Assembly has NO maps or dictionaries.
; You must implement hash tables manually or use 
; an external C library.
; Basic lookup table:
lookup_table:
    dq .handler1, .handler2
maps.notes: No built-in maps exist. Developers rely on simple jump tables, linear searches, or integrate with C libraries for complex data structures.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.code:
call open_file
    test rax, rax
    js .error_handler  ; Jump if sign flag set (negative return)
    
    ; Success path
    jmp .done
.error_handler:
    ; Handle error
error_handling.notes: Errors are typically indicated by specific return values (like negative numbers or 0). It is strictly manual checking.

comments.title: Comments & Documentation
comments.notes: Assembly provides comments to document code behavior.

numbers.title: Numbers & Constants
numbers.notes: Assembly supports numeric literals for computation and indexing.

booleans.title: Booleans & Conditions
booleans.notes: Assembly provides boolean conditions for program control flow.

type_casting.title: Type Conversion
type_casting.notes: Assembly converts data between native format representations.

strings.title: Strings & Characters
strings.notes: Assembly represents textual data through string literals and character arrays.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: Assembly formats and joins textual values for display and output.

pattern_matching.title: Conditionals & Branching
pattern_matching.code:
case value of
    1: execute_one()
    default: execute_default()
pattern_matching.notes: Assembly branches execution based on value comparison and conditional expressions.

range.title: Ranges & Intervals
range.notes: Assembly defines intervals and index sequences for bounded processing.

iterators.title: Iteration & Loops
iterators.notes: Assembly iterates across collections and sequence elements.

oop_classes.title: Structures & Modules
oop_classes.notes: Assembly organizes data and behavior through structures or modular components.

lists.title: Collections & Arrays
lists.notes: Assembly stores sequence data in indexed lists or arrays.

tuples.title: Records & Pairs
tuples.notes: Assembly groups related fields into lightweight composite pairs or records.

sets.title: Sets & Uniqueness
sets.notes: Assembly tracks unique values without duplicate entries.

modules_import.title: Libraries & Modules
modules_import.notes: Assembly organizes external libraries and code units into modular namespaces.
